question.text: In an experiment to measure the speed of sound by a resonating air column, a tuning fork of frequency <math><mn>500</mn><mi> </mi><mi>H</mi><mi>z</mi></math> is used. The length of the air column is varied by changing the level of water in the resonance tube. Two successive resonances are heard at air columns of length <math><mn>50.7</mn><mi> </mi><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi><mi> </mi><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>d</mi><mi> </mi><mn>83.9</mn><mi> </mi><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></math> . Which of the following statements is (are) true?

options.text: The speed of sound determined from this experiment is  <math><mn>332</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi><msup><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>
The end correction in this experiment is  <math><mn>0.9</mn><mi> </mi><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></math>
The wavelength of the sound wave is  <math><mn>66.4</mn><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></math>
The resonance at  <math><mn>50.7</mn><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></math>  corresponds to the fundamental harmonic

solution.text:
Let n1 harmonic is corresponding to 50.7 cm and  n2 harmonic is corresponding 83.9 cm . since both one consecutive harmonics.
∴  There difference =λ2
∴ λ2=83.9-50.7cm
λ2=33.2 cm
λ=66.4 cm
∴ λ4=16.6cm
length corresponding to fundamental mode must be close to λ4 and 50.7 cm must be an odd multiple of this length 16.6 × 3 = 49.8 cm . therefore  50.7 is 3rd harmonic
If end correction is e, then
e+50.7=3λ4
e=49.8-50.7=0.9cm
Speed of sound, c=fλ
∴  v=500×66.4cm/sec=332.000m/sec
